name: card-families batch (3 components + 1 variant)
decision: The owner asked for a survey of card kinds across enterprise design systems and promo pages, then for the result to be BUILT and wired into the system so an agent can pick a card by what the content is. The survey (31 families, screen-specs/card-rules.json) measured the system against them: it covers the card as a carrier of CONTENT and barely covers the card as a carrier of a DECISION. These are the three parts that gap needs, plus the variant that makes a KPI card say whether the number is good.
need: Queue 1 of the survey: the families the products already ask for. `kpi` cannot be built at all (Stat has value and label, no comparison), `analytical` has no chart part of any kind, `option` has no selectable surface (LinkTile navigates and demands a menu), `action` has nothing — a card that asks a question and takes the answer in place is half of enterprise card usage and the system has never had it.

consideredAlternatives.whyNot: A value against a target on a fixed scale, not a value over time; a KPI's trend has no maximum.
Both say how far along, neither says what the shape of the number was.
Navigates on click and requires an overflow menu. A selectable tile changes a value in a form and must survive the next click.

consideredAlternatives.ref: Chip / Radio / Checkbox in a Grid
consideredAlternatives.whyNot: Right for words, wrong for a choice that carries an icon, a description and a price; the surface has to be the control (Carbon selectable tile).
The part nobody hand-rolls correctly is the resolved state: after approve or decline the card must state the outcome, or the reader answers twice.
Stays until resolved and carries a message, not a request addressed to this reader with its own fields and outcome.

components.name: Sparkline
components.why: The trend part of a KPI card and the whole of the analytical card's first form. Pure SVG, no dependency, no axes: shape only, with the last point marked because that is the one the reader is standing on.

components.name: SelectableTile
components.why: A card as a form control: single or multiple choice, the whole surface is the target, the state is visible and keyboard-reachable. Carbon separates it from the clickable tile because the two look alike and behave nothing alike.

components.name: ActionCard
components.why: A question put to this reader, answered in place, with the outcome stated on the same surface afterwards. Adaptive Cards' shape, which the system has never had.

variants.why: A KPI is four layers: label, value, comparison, and a visual anchor. Stat had two. `delta` carries the comparison with its own direction and tone; `trend` takes a <Sparkline> so the tile is complete without a wrapper.
